Nottoway Indian Tribe of Virginia

The Nottoway Indian Tribe of Virginia presents a continuing community whose public historical work is centered in Capron and Southampton County. A named Tribal author’s account of Edith Turner and the Tribe’s interpretive-center page connect earlier leadership with contemporary cultural and educational work. This route is distinct from the broader Nottoway guide and the Cheroenhaka (Nottoway) Indian Tribe.

01

Remembering Edith Turner

André Williams connects Turner’s nineteenth-century political and language work with contemporary Nottoway cultural life. He describes language recording and petitions as parts of her wider leadership. This is a named Tribal author’s interpretation, rather than a newly examined original manuscript or a current language-fluency claim.

Read the sources [1] Nottoway Indian Tribe of Virginia

02

A community-supported place of public history

The Tribe dates its Community House and Interpretive Center opening to May 2012. Its public account describes family support, exhibits and educational programming that connect trade, colonial pressure and continuing identity. The account identifies a living institution; current opening arrangements and program results are separate questions.
